11.ai_answer: Monitoring maternal weight gain is crucial for optimal pregnancy outcomes. Appropriate weight gain (typically 11-16 kg for normal BMI) supports fetal development, placental function, and maternal tissue expansion. Insufficient gain increases risks of preterm birth, low birth weight, and developmental delays. Excessive gain elevates risks of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia, cesarean delivery, macrosomia, and childhood obesity in offspring. Guidelines are individualized based on pre-pregnancy BMI.

12.ai_answer: Plasma lipoproteins are spherical particles with a hydrophobic core containing triglycerides and cholesterol esters, surrounded by an amphipathic shell of phospholipids, free cholesterol, and apolipoproteins. This structure enables transport of water-insoluble lipids through aqueous blood. Different classes (chylomicrons, VLDL, LDL, HDL) vary in density and function: chylomicrons transport dietary lipids, VLDL carries endogenous triglycerides, LDL delivers cholesterol to tissues, and HDL mediates reverse cholesterol transport.
